name: Kube Node Monitor
description: Your Kubernetes cluster's health, right in the GNOME top bar, so you don't have to keep a terminal or dashboard open. A dot on the panel goes amber or red when a node degrades or drops; open the menu for per-node readiness, how long each has been up or down, its role or failure reason, and live CPU/memory usage (with metrics-server). It uses the kubectl and kubeconfig you already have, switches context in one click, and can notify you when a node flips Ready or NotReady. Click a node to copy its 'kubectl describe node' command to the clipboard. Read-only: it never changes your cluster.
